attempts.summary: Implemented router-on-a-stick VLAN segmentation for node1/node2/node3's shared trunk link using an Ansible playbook run from the designated control_node (node4). node1 (VyOS) got 802.1Q sub-interfaces eth1.10 (10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.1/24) via native configure/commit/save. node2 was placed on tagged VLAN 10 (enp8s0.10, 10.10.10.11/24) and node3 on tagged VLAN 20 (enp8s0.20, 10.10.20.12/24) via community.general.nmcli, each with a specific static route to the other VLAN's subnet via node1 (not a competing default route). Verified true inter-VLAN routing (not bridging) via a tcpdump capture on node1's trunk interface showing ICMP packets ingress-tagged VLAN 10 and egress re-tagged VLAN 20 (TTL decrement confirms routing hop). Bootstrapped Ansible SSH access first (created an 'antrieb' user with node4's key on node2/node3; added node4's key to VyOS user 'vyos' via native VyOS config), since no Ansible-reachable credentials pre-existed. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all four managed nodes, confirming changed boot_id/uptime and full recovery of VLAN configuration, routing, and (for node4) SSH/ansible connectivity after each restart.
